aim.definition: To calculate a maneuver that makes the flight go through a given aim point.

aimPoint.definition: The point in the B-plane through which the approach asymptote of the spacecraft goes.

altitude.definition: The distance from the center of a body minus the equatorial radius of the body.

anchor.definition: The state of the spacecraft immediately after a maneuver, as the flight solver calculated it. The propagation continues from this state, thus all computers give the same flight.

apoapsis.definition: The point of an orbit that is farthest from the central body.

approach.definition: The part of a flyby or of an arrival before the closest approach.

apsis.definition: The nearest point or the farthest point of an orbit from the central body.

arc.definition: A part of a trajectory between two times, for example between two maneuvers.

argumentOfPeriapsis.definition: The angle in the orbit plane from the ascending node to the periapsis.

arrival.definition: The encounter with the last body of a plan.

ascendingNode.definition: The point at which an orbit goes through the reference plane from south to north.

asymptote.definition: A straight line that a hyperbolic orbit comes nearer to when the distance from the body increases.

atmosphericDrag.definition: The force of the atmosphere of a body on a spacecraft that moves through it.

attitude.definition: The directions of the axes of the spacecraft.

au.definition: A unit of length. 1 au is 149 597 870.7 km.

barycenter.definition: The center of mass of a group of bodies.

body.definition: An object of the solar system: the Sun, a planet, a dwarf planet, a moon, an asteroid or a comet.

bPlane.definition: The plane through the center of a body that is perpendicular to the approach asymptote. B·T and B·R are the coordinates of the aim point in this plane.

bPlaneCoordinates.definition: The two numbers B·T and B·R. They give the position of the aim point along the T axis and the R axis of the B-plane. The T axis is in the ecliptic plane.

branch.definition: One of the two solutions of the Lambert problem that have the same number of revolutions.

burn.definition: An operation of the engine that changes the velocity of the spacecraft.

c3.definition: The launch energy: the square of the speed at infinity relative to the launch body, in km²/s².

cannonballModel.definition: A model of the spacecraft for the radiation pressure: a sphere with one area and one reflectivity coefficient.

ccsds.definition: The Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems. It publishes the OEM and OPM file formats.

center.definition: The body or point that is the origin of the coordinates.

centralBody.definition: The body at the center of an orbit: the spacecraft moves about this body.

chebyshevFit.definition: A set of polynomials that gives the position of a body in each time interval.

closestApproach.definition: The point of a flyby at which the distance to the body is a minimum.

converge.definition: To get nearer to the solution in each iteration, until the error is less than the limit.

cruise.definition: The part of a flight between two encounters.

dampedNewton.definition: An iteration that calculates each step from the derivatives of the error. If the full step does not decrease the error, the method uses a smaller part of the step.

de440.definition: A planet ephemeris of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory. It is the source of the planet positions of this application.

deltaV.definition: The change of the velocity that a burn gives. The sum of the velocity changes is the cost of a mission.

departure.definition: The start of the motion of the spacecraft from a body: at the launch, or after a flyby.

differentialEvolution.definition: A global search method that changes a group of solutions step by step.

dla.definition: The angle between the launch asymptote and the equator of J2000.

dsm.definition: A large maneuver between two encounters that is a part of the plan.

eccentricity.definition: A number that gives the shape of an orbit: 0 for a circle, less than 1 for an ellipse, more than 1 for a hyperbola.

eclipj2000.definition: The frame of the ecliptic and equinox of J2000. Its XY plane is the plane of the orbit of the Earth.

ecliptic.definition: The plane of the orbit of the Earth about the Sun.

encounter.definition: A point of a plan at which the spacecraft is at a body: the launch, a flyby or the arrival.

entry.definition: An arrival at which the spacecraft goes into the atmosphere of the body.

ephemeris.definition: Data that gives the positions and velocities of bodies as a function of time.

epoch.definition: The time to which a set of orbit elements or a state applies.

equationsOfMotion.definition: The equations that give the acceleration of the spacecraft from the forces of the force model.

equinox.definition: The direction from the Earth to the Sun when the Sun goes from south to north through the plane of the equator of the Earth. In the frame ECLIPJ2000, the X axis points to the equinox of J2000.

escapeHyperbola.definition: The hyperbolic orbit about the launch body on which the spacecraft moves after the launch burn.

exposure.definition: The brightness adjustment of a camera. The 3D view adjusts the exposure to the sunlight at each body.

fixedStep.definition: A time step that has the same length between all samples of a table.

flight.definition: The trajectory of a mission in the full force model, with its maneuvers.

flightSolver.definition: The part of the engine that calculates a flight from a plan.

flyby.definition: A motion of the spacecraft near a body that does not become an orbit about that body.

forceModel.definition: The set of forces that the propagation includes.

frame.definition: A set of three axes. The components of positions and velocities are along these axes.

gm.definition: The gravitational parameter of a body: the product of the gravitational constant and the mass, in km³/s².

gravityAssist.definition: A flyby that changes the velocity of the spacecraft relative to the Sun with no propellant.

heliocentric.definition: Relative to the center of the Sun.

hermiteInterpolation.definition: An interpolation with a polynomial that agrees with the positions and the velocities of the samples.

hohmann.definition: The transfer between two circular orbits in one plane that has the minimum velocity change for two burns.

horizons.definition: The ephemeris service of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory. It is the source of the reference values of this application.

icrf.definition: The International Celestial Reference Frame. Its axes agree with the equator and equinox of J2000 to a very small angle.

impulse.definition: A velocity change in zero time: the model of a burn in this application.

inclination.definition: The angle between the orbit plane and the reference plane.

integrate.definition: To calculate the solution of the equations of motion step by step from a start state.

integrator.definition: The numerical method that integrates the equations of motion step by step.

interpolate.definition: To calculate a value at a time between the samples of a table.

interpolation.definition: The calculation of a value at a time between the samples of a table or between the steps of the integrator.

j2.definition: The number that gives the effect of the equatorial bulge of a body on its gravity.

julianDate.definition: A time as a count of days with a decimal fraction. The Julian date of the epoch J2000 is 2 451 545.0 in TT.

lambert.definition: The problem to find the two-body orbit that connects two positions in a given time.

launch.definition: The first encounter of a plan: the spacecraft starts its flight from the parking orbit about the launch body.

launchWindow.definition: A range of launch dates for which the velocity change of a transfer is near its minimum.

launchWindowMap.definition: A map of a quantity of the transfer as a function of the launch date and the arrival date. Its other name is porkchop plot.

leapSecond.definition: One more second at the end of some UTC days. It keeps UTC near the rotation of the Earth.

leg.definition: The part of a plan between two encounters.

lightTime.definition: The time in which light goes from one point to a different point.

longitudeOfNode.definition: The angle in the reference plane from the X axis to the point where the orbit goes up through that plane.

maneuver.definition: A change of the velocity of the spacecraft that a burn gives.

meanAnomaly.definition: An angle that increases at a constant rate from 0 at the periapsis to 360° after one period.

mission.definition: A spacecraft, its plan and, after the calculation, its flight.

nelderMead.definition: A local search method that does not use derivatives.

noiseFloor.definition: The level below which a search cannot find a signal.

obliquity.definition: The angle between the plane of the equator of the Earth and the ecliptic.

oem.definition: The Orbit Ephemeris Message of CCSDS: a text file with a table of states.

opm.definition: The Orbit Parameter Message of CCSDS: a text file with one state and a list of maneuvers.

optimize.definition: To change the free values of a plan until the cost is a minimum.

optimizer.definition: The part of the engine that optimizes a plan.

orbit.definition: The path of a body or a spacecraft that gravity controls.

orbitElements.definition: A set of six numbers that gives a two-body orbit and the position on it at an epoch. Examples are the semi-major axis, the eccentricity and the inclination.

orbitInsertion.definition: The burn at the periapsis that changes a flyby into an orbit about the body.

orbitNormal.definition: The direction that is perpendicular to the orbit plane, along the vector r × v.

osculatingElements.definition: The elements of the two-body orbit that has the position and velocity of the body at one time.

parkingOrbit.definition: The low circular orbit from which the spacecraft starts its flight.

patchedConic.definition: A model in which the path is a sequence of two-body orbits: about the Sun between the bodies, about a body during an encounter.

periapsis.definition: The point of an orbit that is nearest to the central body.

period.definition: The time of one revolution of an orbit.

perturbation.definition: A force that makes the motion different from a two-body orbit.

phaseAngle.definition: The angle about the central body from the departure body to the arrival body, in the ecliptic plane. It is positive in the prograde direction.

plan.definition: The design of a mission in the patched-conic model: a sequence of encounters with their dates.

prograde.definition: In the direction of the motion of the planets about the Sun.

propagate.definition: To calculate a trajectory forward or backward in time from one state.

propagation.definition: The calculation of a trajectory forward or backward in time from one state.

propellant.definition: The material that the engine uses to change the velocity of the spacecraft.

pumpAngle.definition: The angle between the velocity of a planet and the speed at infinity vector of the spacecraft.

radiationPressure.definition: The small force of the sunlight on the spacecraft.

reflectivityCoefficient.definition: The number by which the cannonball model multiplies the force of the sunlight on the area of the spacecraft.

relativityTerm.definition: The correction of the gravity of the Sun from general relativity.

rendezvous.definition: An arrival at which a burn gives the spacecraft the velocity of the body.

retrograde.definition: Opposite to the direction of the motion of the planets about the Sun.

revolution.definition: One full turn of an orbit about the central body.

rla.term: Right ascension of the launch asymptote (RLA)
rla.definition: The angle of the launch asymptote along the equator of J2000, from the X axis of the ICRF.

rocketEquation.definition: The relation between a velocity change, the specific impulse and the mass before and after the burn.

rtn.definition: A local frame: R along the position, N along the orbit normal, T completes the frame.

semiMajorAxis.definition: One half of the longest diameter of an elliptical orbit. It gives the size and the energy of the orbit.

soi.definition: The volume around a body in which the gravity of that body controls the motion more than the gravity of the Sun.

spacecraft.definition: A vehicle that moves in space.

specificImpulse.definition: The ratio of the thrust of an engine to the weight flow of its propellant, in seconds. A higher value gives more velocity change from the same propellant mass.

state.definition: The position and the velocity at one time.

stateVector.definition: The three components of the position and the three components of the velocity at one time.

synodicPeriod.definition: The time after which two bodies have the same relative position about the Sun again.

tai.definition: International Atomic Time: a time scale with no leap seconds.

target.definition: The body to which a mission goes.

targeter.definition: The part of the engine that aims a maneuver at an encounter.

tcm.definition: A small maneuver that corrects the path to the next aim point.

tdb.definition: Barycentric Dynamical Time: the time scale of the planet ephemeris. It is different from TT by less than 2 ms.

timeScale.definition: A system to count time, for example UTC or TDB.

nominalRadius.definition: A radius that the application uses for a body with no radius in the database. It is not a measured value.

trueScale.definition: A view with one scale for all sizes and all distances.

tisserandGraph.definition: A graph of the orbits that a spacecraft can get from flybys of each planet at a constant speed at infinity.

tisserandParameter.definition: A quantity of an orbit that a flyby of a planet on a circular orbit does not change.

tolerance.definition: The largest error that the integrator accepts in one step.

tour.definition: A plan with one or more flybys between the launch and the arrival.

trajectory.definition: The path of the spacecraft as a function of time.

transfer.definition: The orbit on which the spacecraft goes from one body to a different body.

trueAnomaly.definition: The angle in the orbit plane from the periapsis to the position.

turnAngle.definition: The angle between the approach asymptote and the departure asymptote of a flyby.

twoBody.definition: The orbit in which the only force is the gravity of one central body.

utc.definition: Coordinated Universal Time: the civil time scale. It has leap seconds.

variableStep.definition: A step of the integrator with a length that the integrator changes to keep the error below the tolerance.

velocityBudget.definition: The list of the velocity changes of a mission and their sum.

vinf.definition: The speed of the spacecraft relative to a body, far from the body, on a hyperbolic orbit.

vnb.definition: A local frame: V along the velocity, N along the orbit normal, B completes the frame.
